routes.label: Use cumulative block counts to locate both median entries.

question: In the following list of numbers, the integer \(n\) appears \(n\) times in the list for \(1\leq n\leq200.\) \[ \begin{aligned} &1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,4,4,\ldots,\\ &200,200,\ldots,200 \end{aligned} \] What is the median of the numbers in this list?
solution:
Locate the middle positions by counting how many entries occur through each block. There are
\[
1+2+\cdots+200=\frac{200\cdot201}{2}=20{,}100
\]
entries, so the median is the average of entries \(10{,}050\) and \(10{,}051\).

The block of \(n\)'s ends at position \(n(n+1)/2\). The block of \(141\)'s ends at \(141\cdot142/2=10{,}011\), while the block of \(142\)'s ends at \(142\cdot143/2=10{,}153\).

Both middle positions lie in the block of \(142\)'s. Their average is \(\boxed{142}\), choice C. With repeated blocks, cumulative counts locate the median without writing the list.
